title: P02: momentum-only Muon without Nesterov lookahead
description: P02 follow-up: use the EMA momentum buffer directly as the input to Muon orthogonalization instead of mixing it with the instantaneous gradient via Nesterov lookahead. Smoother matrix-update directions may preserve reusable proof features and improve the policy handed to fixed downstream expert iteration.
hypothesis: Incumbent 043 scores 282/275/269 (exact mean 275.333333). Earlier P02 momentum-coefficient changes to 0.90 and 0.98 failed on the older 034 baseline, but both retained Nesterov lookahead; no existing experiment removes lookahead. With momentum fixed at 0.95, the incumbent direction before orthogonalization is 0.05*g + 0.95*m_new, where m_new=0.95*m_old+0.05*g. This experiment uses m_new alone, reducing the instantaneous-gradient contribution from 0.0975 to 0.05 without changing the EMA recurrence. Less reactive hidden-matrix directions may give fixed RL more transferable features; alternatively, removing lookahead may slow useful adaptation. Orthogonalization makes the direction change nonlinear, so this is not an LR-equivalent control. Only the downstream three-seed mean decides keep/discard; validation loss is diagnostic.
expected_delta: Conditional on improvement, +3 to +15 dev-transfer solves at length >=7 versus exact baseline mean 275.333333; plausible downside -10 to -40. Expect negligible throughput change (one elementwise blend removed), no model-size or inference-latency change, and unchanged fixed 300-second pretraining/1200-second total budgets.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After updating EMA momentum, reshape each QKV momentum direction to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No instantaneous-gradient/Nesterov blend and no extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum coefficient and weight decay stay unchanged.
muon.direction: m_new = 0.95*m_old + 0.05*gradient; orthogonalize m_new directly rather than 0.05*gradient + 0.95*m_new

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. All 16 hidden matrices: qkv (768,256), proj (256,256), fc1 (1024,256), fc2 (256,1024) in each of four blocks. QKV initialized jointly. Embedding, readout, biases and LayerNorm retain their original draws/values. No reinitialization during RL.
